1.title: Park cars face to face
1.say: Drive the two cars nose to nose with fronts close but not touching. Turn off both engines. Set the brakes hard.
placements: good running car → nose to nose facing dead car with fronts close but not touching and both engines off; in the video: red car on grass edge
dead car that will not start → nose to nose facing good car with fronts close but not touching and both engines off; in the video: black car in parking lot
watch_for: cars parked too far so cables cannot reach, if the cables pull tight repark closer with fronts nearer
engine left on with dash lights still glowing, if you see lights or hear the engine turn the key off
1.check_yourself: It should look like two fronts almost touching with both engines quiet and both hoods ready to open.
1.safety: Set the brakes hard so neither car can roll.

2.title: Open hoods and find batteries
2.say: Open both hoods. Prop them up safely. Find the boxy battery in each front corner near the headlights.
placements: hood of good car → raised open over front engine space and held up; in the video: red hood up
hood of dead car → raised open over front engine space and held up with stick; in the video: black hood up held by wood stick
boxy battery of good car → in front corner of engine space near headlight; in the video: side of red car engine space
boxy battery of dead car → in front corner of engine space near headlight; in the video: side of black car engine space near yellow fluid bottle
watch_for: mixing up the battery with the washer bottle or air box, if the box has no thick posts marked plus and minus it is not the battery
hood not propped and can fall, if the hood wobbles push the prop until it locks
2.check_yourself: It should look like both hoods standing open with a big boxy battery seen in each front corner.
2.safety: Keep fingers clear of the heavy hood edge so it cannot pinch you.

3.title: Clip red clamps to plus posts
3.say: Clip the first red clamp to the plus post of the dead battery. Clip the other red clamp to the plus post of the working battery. Wiggle both red clamps so they grip tight and cannot slip.
placements: first red clamp on red wire → plus post of dead battery usually marked plus or under red cover; in the video: post of black battery in black car with red cover lifted
second red clamp on red wire → plus post of good battery usually marked plus or under red cover; in the video: post of battery in red car engine bay
watch_for: red clamp on the minus post, if the post is marked minus move the red clamp to the plus side
red clamp loose and rocking, if you can wiggle it off squeeze it tighter until it cannot move
3.check_yourself: It should look like a red clamp biting the plus post on each battery with the red wire running between the cars.
3.safety: Keep the red clamps from touching each other or any bare metal while you work.

4.title: Clip black clamps to minus and metal
4.say: Clip one black clamp to the minus post of the working battery. Clip the last black clamp to bare metal on the dead car. Choose a spot away from the battery and moving belts.
placements: black clamp on black wire → minus post of good battery usually marked minus; in the video: battery in red car engine bay
black clamp on black wire → bare unpainted metal bolt on frame of dead car away from battery; in the video: bare metal above headlight in black car engine bay
watch_for: black clamp on the minus post of the dead battery, if both clamps are on the dead battery move the last black clamp to bare metal instead
black clamp on paint or plastic or near belts, if there is no shiny metal bite pick a clean bolt on the frame
4.check_yourself: It should look like one black clamp on the working battery minus post and the last black clamp biting bare shiny metal on the dead car.
4.safety: Clip the last black clamp to bare metal never to the dead minus post.

5.title: Start working car to charge
5.say: Start the working car engine with its key. Leave it running for a few minutes to charge.
placements: key of working car → key hole beside steering wheel turned to start with dash lights on then left running; in the video: tan dash of red car with key turned
watch_for: starting the dead car too early, if the dead car is cranked before charging wait a few more minutes with the working car running
working car stalled or turned off, if dash lights go out restart it and keep it running
5.check_yourself: It should look like the working car dash lit with its engine humming while the cables stay still for a few minutes.
5.safety: Keep hands and clothes clear of spinning belts while the engine runs.

6.title: Start dead car and remove cables
6.say: Start the dead car engine with its key. Lift the red and black clamps clear and apart. Leave the revived car running for a few minutes.
placements: key of dead car → key hole beside steering wheel turned to start; in the video: dash of black car with key turned
black clamp from bare metal on dead car → lifted clear of engine space and held apart from other clamps; in the video: lifted off front frame above headlight
black clamp from minus post of working car → lifted clear of engine space and held apart; in the video: lifted off red car battery
red clamp from plus post of working car → lifted clear of engine space and held apart; in the video: lifted off red car battery
red clamp from plus post of dead car → lifted clear of engine space and held apart; in the video: lifted off black car battery
watch_for: clamps touching each other when removing, if you see a spark keep each clamp in separate hands apart
turning off the revived car right away, if it was just started leave it running a few minutes so it does not die again
6.check_yourself: It should look like both engines humming with all clamps off and the wires clear of both front spaces.
6.safety: Keep the loose clamps apart so they never touch each other.
